paragraphs: Friend, here's what hit me. Jesus tells the Twelve what's waiting in Jerusalem: condemned, mocked, flogged, crucified, and then raised to life on the third day (Matthew 20:18-19). Right after that, a mother kneels and asks that her two sons sit at His right and left in His kingdom (Matthew 20:20-21). I think that's the most human moment in the chapter, and I say that as somebody who has also been busy with the wrong thing at the wrong time.

Jesus answers, "You do not know what you are asking," and then He turns the whole thing upside down (Matthew 20:22). The rulers of the Gentiles lord it over people, but He says, "It shall not be this way among you" (Matthew 20:25-26). In His kingdom, greatness is measured by who's willing to serve, not by who sits closest to the throne. So the question for you and me is not how high we can climb, but who we can lift today.

Jesus doesn't ask us to do anything He hasn't done first. He says the Son of Man "did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many" (Matthew 20:28). The One with every right to the best seat took the lowest place for us. So when you serve somebody this week, quietly, with nobody clapping, you're following the best Master there ever was.
